items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There were other musicians, like Charlie Elgar and Hypolite Charles

ctx.x: Sugar Johnny. I’ll have to check and see. I’m working on a Dodds thing right now.

Dodds was in Chicago. He was the first one in Chicago to keep the New Orleans tradition other than King Oliver and Louis Armstrong. There were other musicians, like Charlie Elgar and Hypolite Charles . . . no, not Hypolite. Was head of the Chicago union. Him and his wife played piano. Can’t think of their names.
Did you see people like . . . and hear King Oliver and them perform before they went up to Chicago?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Charles Elgar and them people, they... I guess they had seen a lot.

ctx.x: But the people who went through that disappointment, like you said, Charles Elgar and them people, they... I guess they had seen a lot. And he was a high-class man.

Yeah, he was a high-class man. Yeah, he did... Mister Elgar did a great deal for Chicago, the Black musicians of Chicago until he died. He almost lived... He quite a life -- past ninety. And he got involved with the union, with those bands, with the union trust fund. And he was always for helping young ones, a couple of young cello players... Guys like Richard Davis came out from under Mister Elgar.
